results.summary: This project implements a mini MOSbius analog chip in a 3x2 Tiny Tapeout slot. It contains programmable NMOS and PMOS transistors, differential pairs, OTAs, and current sources. Six buses with transmission gates allow interconnection of the blocks, programmed by a shift register. Silicon tests confirmed working inverter, differential amplifier, ring oscillator, and current source configurations.

results.summary_before: This design implements a register bank that can be accessed through either an SPI or an I2C serial interface, with a digital input selecting which interface is active. It is used by writing and reading registers over the selected bus, and the first register is documented as controlling LEDs on the demo board. External hardware may include 2k2 pull-up resistors on the I2C SDA and SCL lines, and testers have used a Bus Pirate and a Pico with internal pull-ups to exercise both interfaces. Silicon tests confirmed read and write access over SPI and I2C, including multi-byte transfers and cross-interface access to the same registers.
results.summary: This design implements a configurable ring oscillator using manually instantiated inverter cells. The ring oscillator or an external clock drives a counter that counts up to 3000. A VGA sync generator uses the upper bits of the counter to produce colored bars on a VGA display. Silicon tests confirmed VGA output and a ring oscillator frequency of about 78 MHz.
